name: Tridemism
summary: Tridemism, or the Three Principles of the People (Sanminzhuyi), is Sun Yat-sen's programme of nationalism (ending foreign domination and building a unified Chinese nation), democracy (a republic with four popular powers and a five-branch government, reached through a period of tutelage) and livelihood (land-value taxation, limited private capital and state-run key industries to prevent extreme inequality). It rejects Marxist class struggle in favour of cooperation, curbs individual liberty for national unity, and draws on Confucian virtues and the Datong ideal.
scope: Sun Yat-sen's doctrine as set out in the 1905-1906 Tongmenghui/Minbao statements and the 1924 lectures, with the Kuomintang's state version as it existed in the Republic of China; it excludes the Chinese Communist Party's "New Three Principles" reading and later Taiwanese liberal reinterpretations except where noted. Chiang Kai-shek's own additions are covered by the separate Chiangism profile.

sources.title: Sun Yat-sen, The Three Principles of the People (excerpt)
sources.author: Sun Yat-sen; Center for History and New Media
sources.usedFor: Sun on liberty: China as a sheet of loose sand, with individual liberty to be reduced for national unity.

sources.title: On New Democracy
sources.author: Mao Zedong (marxists.org)
sources.usedFor: A later reading of Sun's principles: alliance with Russia and Communists, land to the tiller, state ownership of major banks and industry with private capital allowed.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Livelihood covers food, clothing, housing and transport provided with state help and welfare, so health care is a plausible extension, but the sources never mention it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Livelihood aims at sharing national income gains with ordinary citizens, but no wage-setting policy appears in the sources I read; inferred from that goal.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sun wanted private capital limited and the state to run communications, mining and manufacturing, so he did not trust markets alone to serve livelihood.

public-ownership.rationale: Sun wanted the state to run key sectors such as communications and mining, and Mao's reading has the state owning major banks and railways so private capital cannot dominate livelihood.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The land-value tax takes the unearned rise in land values for the public, and livelihood aims to prevent extreme inequality, so heavier burdens on the rich fit.

unions-good.rationale: The new principles include assistance to workers and peasants, but unions as such are not discussed in the sources; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Sun limited private capital and had the state hold the right to buy land at its declared price and capture land-value increases, so property yields to public goals.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Sun's principle of regulating capital meant restraining private enterprise so it would not dominate people's livelihood.

cut-welfare.rationale: Livelihood was framed as social welfare and care for the aged, young and disabled in the Datong ideal, which opposes cutting benefits.

worker-ownership.rationale: Sun rejected class struggle and preferred state ownership of key industries plus limited private capital, with no workplace cooperatives programme in the sources.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Sun's emphasis on order, unity and curbing liberty makes security surveillance acceptable, but the issue is anachronistic and unaddressed.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Sun's Confucian moral revival and the KMT's moral campaigns suggest opposition, though drugs are not discussed in the sources; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents had no recorded position on hate speech; Sun curbed liberty for unity, while stressing equal standing of groups, so it is genuinely open.

strong-leader.rationale: Sun gave experts real discretion and endorsed party tutelage, but also built five branches and popular powers to check government, so adherents split.

state-harmful.rationale: Sun built a five-branch government and a unitary state under tutelage, so the state is central and necessary to the doctrine.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; Sun's priority on order and state authority over individual liberty suggests support for tight control.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed directly, but the doctrine begins with military rule and gives the state a strong role in national unity and defence against imperialism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed; the Confucian moral revival Sun called for points against legalisation.

decide-locally.rationale: Sun backed county-level autonomy as a step to democracy but opposed federalism and wanted a unitary state, so the answer splits.

rehabilitation.rationale: Sources never address penal philosophy, and Confucian moral education points one way while order points another.

traditional-family.rationale: Sun wanted clan loyalties broadened into national unity and revived Confucian virtues, which rest on family morality.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; Confucian traditionalism implies disagreement, though Sun's own era had no debate on it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Sun feared falling Chinese birth rates against the West, so he would resist easy abortion, but he never addressed it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Religion appears only as one natural force forming a nation; the doctrine is secular and Confucian-moral rather than religious.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Sun's concern was ending foreign domination of China, not remedies for racial injustice within states.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources are silent; Sun's era and Confucian outlook point against, though this is an inference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Sun explicitly called for reviving traditional Chinese virtues and political thought, citing the Great Learning, as part of rebuilding national spirit.

gradual-change.rationale: Sun was a revolutionary who overthrew the Qing and planned staged tutelage, not a defender of established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Sun's China was a source of emigrants and his concern was demographic strength.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sun saw the world as dominated by Western might and treaties as unequal, so he stressed national sovereignty over international authority.

free-trade.rationale: Sun attacked foreign economic control and unequal treaties and wanted the state to develop industry, so free trade was suspect.

nation-first.rationale: National survival against imperialism was Sun's first principle, though he also spoke of aiding weaker peoples.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sun opposed Western Might-based rule and championed anti-imperialism, but did not address intervention for human rights; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Sun blamed imperial cosmopolitanism for weakening Chinese national spirit and made national unity the goal.

limit-growth.rationale: Sun wanted rapid industrial development and big infrastructure projects like a Yangtze dam, the opposite of limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the sources, though a state-directed approach would not be alien to it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Sun's developmental plans rested on industrialisation and infrastructure to supply livelihood.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic, inferred from Sun's emphasis on state-led industrial and energy development.

revolution-justified.rationale: Sun's Tongmenghui programme called for overthrowing the Qing by revolution and ending monarchy, as set out in his 1906 Minbao speech.

experts-over-public.rationale: Sun separated people's sovereignty from government ability and wanted experts to run government with discretion, though the people keep four powers.

central-planning.rationale: Sun wanted state-run key industries and planned development but kept limited private capital, so full central planning is neither endorsed nor rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: Sun supported mixed state and private ownership, not worker ownership specifically; the statement fits poorly.

land-value-tax.rationale: Sun's land-value tax with self-declared values was central to livelihood, though he did not propose it as replacing most other taxes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Livelihood aimed at preventing concentration of wealth, so heavy inheritance taxation fits, but it is not quoted in the sources.

basic-income.rationale: The doctrine's welfare is tied to national development and Datong care for the needy, not unconditional cash payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Sun's anti-imperialism targeted unequal treaties and foreign economic control and aimed at domestic state-led industrialisation.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Sun explicitly wanted the state to run communications, mining and manufacturing and to direct development with a national plan.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land to the tiller and limiting concentrated capital point to broadly spread holdings, with the state owning the largest enterprises.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Sun rejected Marxism and class struggle and kept private capital, so abolishing wages is outside the doctrine.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Mao's reading has the state owning the major banks, so central banking is retained under state control.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a feature of the sources; Sun rejected class struggle and favoured cooperation, but there is no corporatist bargaining scheme in them.

one-party-rule.rationale: The tutelage period was read as KMT party rule, and the KMT made the doctrine state ideology; Sun did not specify it in writing.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Sun's 1906 speech states China must end centuries of monarchy and establish a democratic republic.

democracy-best.rationale: The principle of democracy aims at a republic with four popular powers, though only after a tutelage period and with experts in office.

direct-votes.rationale: Sun's four popular powers include initiative and referendum, giving citizens direct votes on laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Sun designed a five-branch government with popular powers and no soviet-style basis, and rejected Marxist class politics.

right-to-secede.rationale: Sun opposed federalism and wanted a unitary state, and championed one Zhonghua minzu.

natural-rulers.rationale: Sun separated sovereignty from ability and wanted able experts governing, but also insisted on popular sovereignty; split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Sun's 1906 programme called for revolution against the Qing, rejecting the view that political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Sun contrasted kingly rule with rule by force and criticised Western might, so glorifying war is unlikely; the topic is not directly addressed.

separate-church-state.rationale: The doctrine is secular and does not discuss church-state relations, though common religion is one force building a nation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The legal order rests on the five-power constitution and Confucian moral philosophy, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts, army and examinations are state branches under the five-power constitution.

military-superiority.rationale: Sun sought national defence and equality among nations rather than superiority, though he feared Western might.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sun held nations form from blood kinship, language, livelihood, religion and customs, and expected minorities to assimilate into the Han-centred Zhonghua minzu.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Sun explicitly rejected class struggle as the engine of history, saying the primary force of human evolution is cooperation and not struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Livelihood seeks to prevent extreme inequality but never sought equality of outcomes in general.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Sun expected minorities to assimilate and favoured a unitary state, which cuts against special authority over lands.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Sun denounced imperial powers as exploiting China and demanded repeal of unequal treaties, but reparations are not discussed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Sun praised wangdao and sought Asian solidarity against the West at times, but the sources do not set out a civilisational union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The doctrine stresses a public spirit and cooperation, in the Datong ideal where public and common spirit ruled all under the sky.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Sun argued individual liberty must be curbed so individuals are pressed together into a unified nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Sun's programme treats land and mining as resources for livelihood and development, so nature's value is instrumental; inferred.

limit-population.rationale: Sun feared falling Chinese birth rates relative to the West would risk extinction, so he wanted population to grow.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Sun's plans centred on industrial development as the route to livelihood and national strength.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Sun planned rapid development, but his doctrine valued order and gradual tutelage over disruption of institutions; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic: Sun's era had no such debate and his doctrine gives no principle that settles it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; Sun wanted expert human government balanced by popular powers, not algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine's priority on state order suggests opposing it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Sun's aim was a new republic with constitutional stages, while borrowing Confucian ideals; he did not seek a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Sun's doctrine is itself an ideology yet stresses practical development, so adherents are split.

direct-action.rationale: Sun planned party organisation and tutelage toward constitutional government rather than relying on direct action alone.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; Sun accepted military and party rule as means toward constitutional democracy, which cuts against it.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Sun's livelihood programme aimed at providing food, clothing, housing and transport through industrial development, the opposite of a return to foraging. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Sun planned expert government and state-run industry, which depend on division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Datong envisions care for the aged and needy, but Sun did not set out a need-based distribution rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Livelihood aims at meeting basic needs, yet Sun kept limited private capital and profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Sun called Marx a social pathologist and rejected class-struggle theory, so he did not hold that profit is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Sun rejected Marxist class struggle as not fitting China, and framed the state around the whole people.

collective-farming.rationale: The policy is land to the tiller, giving peasants their own farms rather than collectivising them.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Sun blamed the Western powers' rule of might for imperialism but did not state capitalism as the cause.

taxation-theft.rationale: Sun's land-value tax and state revenue for development are central to livelihood, so he saw taxation as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Sun argued for curbing individual liberty for national unity, beyond the harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Sun rejected Western individual liberty and called China a sheet of loose sand needing group cohesion.

conscription.rationale: Sun's first stage is military government and national defence against imperialism, so conscription is plausible; not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Sun placed the people's four powers at the centre of his democracy principle, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state in Sun's plan runs industries and has examination and control branches, not a customer model.

positive-liberty.rationale: Sun's livelihood principle combined liberty with provision of food, clothing, housing and transport and balanced it against group unity.

media-academia-power.rationale: Sun gave real authority to elected representatives and expert officials under the five-power constitution, not to media or universities; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Sun believed in five hereditary races, but did not rank them or claim ability gaps in the sources I read.

organic-representation.rationale: Sun's representation was through voting with four popular powers and a National Assembly, not guild or family bodies.

total-state.rationale: Sun wanted state control of key industries but kept limited private capital and popular powers, not a state directing all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Sun called China a sheet of loose sand needing to be reformed into a strong nation by reviving traditional virtues and unity.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Sun's aim was ending foreign domination, equality among nations and kingly rather than hegemonic rule.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Sun rejected monarchy and oligarchy, calling for a republic with popular powers.

bound-labor.rationale: Land to the tiller redistributes land to peasants, opposite of binding them to a lord.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's reliance on expert ability suggests knowledge is not purely power.

universal-morality.rationale: Sun appealed to Confucian virtues as universal in the Great Learning's programme, but the sources do not cover this question directly.

single-common-good.rationale: The Datong ideal of a public and common spirit and Sun's rejection of class struggle imply a common good over group interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the doctrine; national self-determination principles are neutral here.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Sun's principles never take up diaspora return, and the nationalism principle could support or not.

revive-national-language.rationale: No language policy appears in the sources, and Chinese was never out of use, so the question hardly applies.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The doctrine has no workplace democracy element and prefers state-led development.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; state-led education and moral instruction suggest disagreement.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Sun's plans relied on foreign loans and state investment for development, but fiscal rules were not debated in his day.

economic-freedom.rationale: Sun curbed private capital, and held liberty must serve the group, so political freedom does not depend on economic freedom for him.

rule-by-example.rationale: Sun invoked the Confucian contrast of kingly rule over rule by force and the Great Learning's self-cultivation of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Sun's nationalism sought to end Qing and foreign domination so that China governs itself, and the 1924 manifesto granted minorities self-determination, but his later Zhonghua minzu view denied separate statehood to Tibetans and Mongols.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic, since the UN did not exist; Sun's anti-imperialism cuts against great-power force but favours Chinese sovereignty.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine mixes scientific development with Confucian moral tradition.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Livelihood is a programme for the Chinese people as a nation, so welfare for citizens first is a natural reading; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed, though the Datong care for the disabled suggests unconditional help for them.

class-collaboration.rationale: Sun said cooperation and not struggle is the main force of human evolution and rejected class struggle for China.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Sun called for reviving traditional virtues and political thought, so he opposed discarding inherited culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Sun called China a hypocolony, praised Soviet Russia as an exception to Western might, and sought allies against imperial powers.

workers-nation.rationale: Sun prioritised national unity over international class solidarity and rejected Marxist internationalism, though workers are to be assisted.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; Confucian traditions and women's participation both appear in KMT history.

ban-interest.rationale: Sun's industrial plans relied on foreign loans and investment, so banning interest is unlikely.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Sun sought equal standing among peoples and assimilation into the Zhonghua minzu, not legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Sun rejected class-struggle analysis and saw the state as an instrument of national development.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; Sun's development plans stressed mining and energy under state direction.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Sun expected minorities to assimilate into the Han-centred Zhonghua minzu, which implies the same for newcomers.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which sought unity and had no such theory.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's system used popular powers and five branches.

national-mission.rationale: Sun spoke of China helping weaker peoples and kingly rule, but did not state a mission to spread its government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources do not address gender hierarchy, and KMT-era views varied between Confucian tradition and women's rights.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not a doctrinal position; Sun built control and examination branches against corruption, but he did not frame elites as corrupt.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Sun's control branch was meant to audit officials, but accountability for past killings was not addressed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Sun explicitly wanted the state to run communications, mining and manufacturing and to provide livelihood.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Sun expected assimilation of minorities into the Han majority, which implies mixing; the topic is not discussed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Sun's democracy invoked liberty, equality, fraternity and sought equal standing for ethnic groups after the Qing fell.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Sun sought national development within China and was not a Marxist internationalist.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The doctrine concerns foreign domination of China, not settler states elsewhere, so it does not decide the question.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Sun's unitary state and common Zhonghua nation imply uniform law, though the issue is not addressed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine does not centre religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a concern in Chinese Sun-ist thought and not mentioned in the sources.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The doctrine is secular and moral rather than religious, but the sources do not mention this.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Sun's tutelage state and anti-imperialist defence imply strengthening the state against hostile powers, though not a Marxist withering-away argument.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The principle of democracy holds that sovereignty rests with the people, though tutelage delays full constitutional government.

trade-surplus.rationale: Sun wanted foreign capital and trade to build China, with no stated export-surplus goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Sun opposed expelling or massacring the Manchus and favoured assimilation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Sun stated that the primary force of human evolution is cooperation and not struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The KMT claimed tutelage as one-party leadership; banning parties against the order fits but is inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's liberty concept was about group freedom from foreign domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Sun split power into five branches and balanced them with four popular powers, though he thought strong legislatures could tyrannise the executive.

vanguard-party.rationale: Sun's tutelage gave the party a guiding role, but he did not frame it as a vanguard of the working class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Livelihood addresses the people's needs generally rather than giving priority to the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Livelihood includes housing but no tenure policy of this kind appears in the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; Sun valued class cooperation but also assistance to workers.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Sun feared low birth rates and attributed poverty to foreign exploitation and inequity, not population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Sun saw China as loose sand needing unity and favoured assimilation, which implies diversity weakens cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sun filled offices through examination and election, in the Examination Yuan.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Sun's tutelage and military stages accepted temporary strong rule, though emergency law is not specified.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Livelihood puts the state in charge of ensuring food, clothing and housing for all, which could include price fixing in scarcity; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed; KMT practice differed from Sun's own writings.

party-commands-army.rationale: The KMT's party army and party-led tutelage are part of the historical record, though Sun did not set it out in the principles.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Immigration was not a concern in Sun's writings, so the doctrine gives no answer.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Sun's five-power constitution says nothing about the pay of officials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The KMT was a disciplined party-led regime, but the sources do not state this rule.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sun prioritised sovereignty restoration against foreign powers.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Sun's five-branch design divided executive power but does not settle command of the armed forces in the sources I read.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The doctrine has no church polity and cannot answer a question about episcopal governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Sun's constitution rests on popular sovereignty and five branches with no clerical authority. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Sun's nationalism supported defending the nation against foreign powers and rejected cosmopolitan class internationalism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Sun promoted traditional virtues but the sources do not discuss censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Sun's constitution does not address term length for the head of state in the sources I read.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is one of the four popular powers Sun listed, with suffrage, initiative and referendum.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Sun allied with Soviet Russia in 1924, so he did not reject alliances in principle, but sought independence.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; Sun kept private property and limited capital.

people-in-arms.rationale: Sun planned military government and a regular army in the first stage.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Mao's reading affirms land to the tiller, but nothing says rural life is morally healthier.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Sun favoured a unitary state and Zhonghua minzu unity, so reuniting a divided nation fits.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Sun valued examination, learning and expert government, so he would not claim the educated are out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Sun contrasted kingly Chinese rule with Western might and held Chinese tradition valuable, implying some ranking.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; order and state authority suggest support.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sun's writings do not discuss school curricula on sex; Confucian morality and modernising education pull in different directions.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Sun admired science and the doctrine is secular; not discussed in the sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Confucian moral revival suggests this, but the sources do not discuss it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Sun defined the nation by blood kinship and customs, favouring descent-based membership.

minority-language-support.rationale: Sun expected minorities to assimilate into the Han majority.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's unitary state favours uniform law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Sun said China had too much individual liberty and needed to press individuals together.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Sun resented foreign economic control and unequal treaties, but debt cancellation is not directly discussed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Sun linked national independence to repealing unequal treaties and ending foreign economic control and built livelihood into the same programme.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Sun's 1924 plan had a People's Congress promulgate the constitution once enough provinces were ready, rather than an immediate assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Sun held liberty must be curbed for national unity and used tutelage to build development before constitutional rule.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sun proposed that Western powers devote military budgets to Chinese infrastructure, but a general duty is not stated.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic, but Sun's emphasis on sovereignty could support national deterrence or not; the sources do not decide.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Sun's five-power design had a different structure; the sources do not decide this.

central-bank-independence.rationale: In Mao's reading of the doctrine the state owns the major banks, which cuts against independent central banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalism's emphasis on territory and unity suggests refusing to cede land, though this is inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Sun's land-value tax passes unearned gains to the state, so property is justified by common benefit.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Sun praised Soviet Russia and Lenin, so he would not call it state capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic, with no environmental doctrine in Sun's livelihood principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Sun sought allies such as Soviet Russia, but a mutual-defence clause is not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Sun's nationalism denounced foreign seizure of Chinese land, but the specific legal view is inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Sun's state is secular and sovereign, but he did not discuss clergy or religious property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not describe a ceremonial head of state, and the KMT leader was party leader.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Sun's unitary state and Zhonghua minzu unity imply preventing secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Sun favoured a uniform unitary state with county autonomy, not special regional systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Sun's 1906 Minbao speech called for ending centuries of monarchy and building a democratic republic, so no sacred head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Livelihood aims at reducing inequality via the land-value tax, so flat taxes sit poorly with it.

character-from-environment.rationale: Sun believed in biological races but also in education and tutelage forming citizens, so the doctrine splits on this.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Sun's five-power constitution binds rulers to the Control and Examination branches and popular recall.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; Sun's priorities were roads, railways, mining and basic livelihood, not space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Sun's design is a five-power plan balanced by popular powers, not the classical few-and-many mixture.

leader-cult.rationale: The KMT built weekly bows to Sun's portrait and readings of his testament into state ritual.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is not discussed in the sources I read.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Sun denied that class struggle drives history and held cooperation is the main force of evolution, so it would not continue under any order he planned.

land-redistribution.rationale: Mao's account of Sun's land to the tiller has landlords' land redistributed to peasants, though Sun's own policy was mostly taxation.

refugee-return.rationale: Not a question Sun's principles take up, as refugee return concerns conflicts outside his programme.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not addressed beyond Sun's wish to regain lost sovereignty.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Sun's doctrine is secular and gives no ground for criminalising change of religion; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress codes for women are absent from Sun's doctrine; inferred disagreement.

common-currency.rationale: Sun's nationalism stresses national sovereignty, but the sources do not discuss monetary unions.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; Sun spoke of five races within one Chinese nation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Sun expected minorities to assimilate into the Han-centred nation.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The doctrine concerns the Chinese nation within China, so it takes no side on diaspora minorities' strategies.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Sun held that the quest for subsistence drives history, though he denied class struggle.

ban-cartels.rationale: Livelihood sought to prevent private capital from dominating the economy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Sun wanted the state to own major banks and run key industries, but bailouts are not discussed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Sun's government had a separate judicial and control branch, but also gave the people popular powers.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Sun's constitution says nothing about quotas for women in public bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Sun sought foreign capital and loans for development, not autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic, with no stated view on international trade standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Sun's public-spirit Datong ideal values moral motives, but he kept material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Sun's own Tongmenghui and KMT used armed uprisings to create a revolution rather than waiting.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Sun's 1906 programme ended monarchy and called for a republic with equal citizens.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Sun called for reviving Chinese virtues and political thought and rebuilding national consciousness, which supports a nation-centred curriculum.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sun attacked imperial rule over China and favoured kingly over might-based rule, though his own domestic tutelage rests on a similar logic of readiness.

patriotic-education.rationale: The KMT made the principles state dogma with weekly bows to Sun's portrait, and the Whampoa address became the national anthem, expressing loyalty education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The doctrine does not concern preferences between racial groups inside a state, as Sun expected assimilation into the Han majority.

public-money-creation.rationale: Mao's reading puts major banks under state ownership, but money creation is not discussed.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Sun hoped to avoid capitalism's evils by regulation, which implies it can be managed, but he did not argue collapse or adaptation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed beyond Sun's concern for Chinese sovereignty.

delink-world-market.rationale: Sun wanted to attract foreign capital, loans and Western help for development, not delink from the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Sun rejected Marxist class analysis, so he would not hold this Leninist thesis, although he called China a hypocolony.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Sun's state-regulating capital and equality among peoples are opposed to unlimited private freedom.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Sun distrusted Western-style individual rights and focused on popular powers and group liberty.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Repealing the unequal treaties was central to Sun's anti-imperialism in the 1920s.

elective-rulers.rationale: Sun's republic would fill the head of state through election, not inheritance, as the monarchy was to end.

minority-veto.rationale: Sun feared China's loose-sand disunity and wanted a unitary state that binds individuals.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Recall and control branches embody accountability, but resisting a ruler is not specifically stated.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Sun feared strong Western legislatures could tyrannise the executive and instead split power among five branches.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not discussed in the sources, and Confucian tradition gives no firm rule.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Sun's principles do not mention animal use, so nothing in the sources fixes an answer.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Datong ideal of public spirit and care for the aged, young and disabled suggests duty of the better-off, but it is not stated as such.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Sun built a nation-building programme calling for citizens to take part, with four popular powers and Great Learning's duties to govern the state.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The claim is a Marxist critique; Sun rejected Marxist analysis and used culture and ritual to build loyalty.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; Sun rejected class-ruler analysis.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Sun called China a hypocolony under foreign economic control, which resembles the claim that the world economy extracts from weaker countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: Sun's examination system chose officials by ability, not birthplace, but the sources do not mention foreign-born candidates.

party-own-road.rationale: Sun's China-first thinking, rejecting Marxism as unfit for China, implies each party finds its own path.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Sun welcomed foreign capital and Western assistance, including a proposal for powers to fund Chinese infrastructure.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Regaining lost Chinese sovereignty and ending unequal treaties was central to Sun's nationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Sun favoured Han-led assimilation and unitary politics, not a special leadership for pre-colonial descendants.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine predates fascism's rise.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Sun praised Lenin and later KMT was anti-communist, so adherents differ and the doctrine is not about this.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is outside the doctrine and the sources do not discuss it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Sun's principles do not address contested monuments, though the KMT valued state memorials to its own founders.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-based social programmes are not addressed in the sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not addressed in the sources I read.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Sun rejected Western individual liberty and parliamentary models as unsuited to China, devising five powers drawn from imperial examination and censorate traditions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Sun's first stage is military government and the KMT ran a military-led tutelage under Chiang.

paid-care-work.rationale: Livelihood includes care ideals in Datong but no scheme of paying domestic labour appears.

filial-duty.rationale: Sun called for reviving traditional Chinese virtues and the Great Learning's family-to-state ethic.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Examination Yuan was explicitly drawn from the imperial civil-service exam to select officials by ability.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Sun opposed foreign economic control and wanted the state to run key sectors such as communications and mining.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed in the sources, and Confucian family values cut against it while modernising reform cut for it.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Recall is one of Sun's four popular powers, though he did not bind elected leaders to constituents.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; a state-guided welfare approach suggests disagreement.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Sun's land policy allowed private ownership with value taxation and state buyback, not use-based tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Sun's constitution gives legislative and control powers to separate branches, but a budget rule is not in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Sun's Zhonghua minzu with assimilation of minorities suggests one common language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Sun resisted foreign control of Chinese land and economy and sought to recover sovereignty from unequal treaties.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination law of this kind is outside the doctrine and not addressed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; Sun wanted material livelihood for all.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The doctrine does not address arming insurgents abroad, though the KMT did receive Soviet aid.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Sun's anti-imperialism opposes domination by great powers.

corporate-influence.rationale: Sun's livelihood principle regulated capital to keep private interests from dominating national life.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sun's concern with foreign control suggests support, but the sources do not mention NGOs.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Sun feared China's falling birth rate relative to the West and wanted national survival through population.

residents-only-property.rationale: Sun opposed foreign control of land through unequal treaties, but local residency limits are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Livelihood aims at provision of basic needs, but a job guarantee is not stated.

democratic-peace.rationale: Sun linked kingly rule to peace and might to war, but the democratic-peace thesis is not in the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Sun stressed duties to the group and unified national discipline, not a right to disobey.

non-intervention.rationale: Sun resented intervention by powers in China, but also sought help from allies like Soviet Russia.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organisation form is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; Sun rejected hostility to all Manchus.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Confucian traditionalism implies strong support for legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Sun's control branch audited officials, but a public right of access to information is not stated.

local-production.rationale: Sun wanted national development and trade with foreign powers, not local self-sufficiency.

informal-organisation.rationale: Sun built the KMT as a disciplined party for revolution and tutelage.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sun's aim was restoring Chinese sovereignty against unequal treaties imposed by other powers.

religious-nation.rationale: Common religion is one force forming a nation, but Sun's nation rests mainly on blood, language and customs.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Sun condemned Western rule by might and sought to end China's subordination to powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Sun's unitary state with state-run industry implies central control of revenue, but this is inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Private ownership is retained under livelihood, including personal property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Sun in 1924 allied with the Communists and the principles sat beside Soviet help, as Mao's reading records.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: A mix of state and private enterprise is Sun's economy, though not for public services specifically.

religion-illusion.rationale: Sun did not hold Marx's view of religion, but the sources do not discuss religion beyond calling it a nation-forming force.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Sun wanted to develop industry and capital, but wanted to prevent capitalism's evils through regulation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Sun's livelihood focuses on national economic development, and no link between women's equality and the economy appears in the sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Datong's care for the aged and young is stated as a social ideal, but whether this is provided by the state or families is not specified.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not mentioned in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Sun denounced unequal treaties but not agreements with minorities.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Datong ideal is universal harmony, not small communes; Sun's plan was a national state.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; the assimilation expectation points toward it but nothing says settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Sun framed livelihood as a path that regulates capital without class struggle, and Mao says China must not copy a European capitalist society either.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nationalism rooted in ethnic kinship and regaining lost territory supports such claims, but it is not discussed specifically.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Sun's principles do not address it, but nothing in them supports denying documented atrocity; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; Confucian traditionalism leans against acceptance, but nothing states criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Sun's tutelage was party rule, but he promised later democracy; KMT practice differed.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The doctrine is secular and has no basis for punishing blasphemy; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Sun denounced imperial exploitation of China as a hypocolony, making this the opposite of his view.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A Muslim religious duty is outside Sun's secular nationalism; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Sun's constitution rests on popular sovereignty, not religious law, so removing rulers for irreligion has no place in it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Sun's four popular powers of suffrage, recall, initiative and referendum aim at direct popular sovereignty.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, which rejected class-based analysis.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life law is not addressed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Sun mixed nationalism, welfare and state industry, with a third course between capitalism and Marxism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Sun rejected Marx as a social pathologist, so he did not take up alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Sun's nation-building included Hui and other peoples within the Chinese nation, so singling out Islam as incompatible is not part of it; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Sun's 1906 speech grounds authority in a republic of the people, not in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not discussed, since the doctrine is secular but Sun did not legislate dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace law of this kind is not addressed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Sun's mixed economy of limited private capital and state industry with welfare resembles this middle path.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Sun's first stage is military government and the doctrine seeks national defence against imperialism. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

rich-first.rationale: Sun wanted shared national income gains but nothing states this staged approach.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Sun allied with Soviet Russia and sought help from powers, though neutrality was not stated.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Sun's republic ended hereditary monarchy in favour of elected office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mao's account has state ownership of major banks, not mutual credit banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sun welcomed foreign loans but resented foreign economic control; no specific stance.

property-franchise.rationale: Sun's four powers include universal suffrage in the people's hands.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The claim is an ecofeminist thesis absent from Sun's doctrine; inferred disagreement.

reification.rationale: Not a Sun-ist concept, as he rejected Marxist analysis.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Sun feared wealth dominating livelihood, but his sources do not mention press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Constitutional government is the final stage of Sun's programme, but the sources do not discuss rule by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: Sun's democracy principle gives popular powers to the whole people.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: the internet postdates Sun, and his four popular powers could be extended or not.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic, and the sources do not describe record publication.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine is not religious.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Sun opposed hostility to minorities and sought unity.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Anachronistic; Sun's People's Congress was elected from counties.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religion is a minor topic in the sources, so no stance on doctrinal reinterpretation can be drawn.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Livelihood regulation of capital and land-value tax aim to stop concentration of wealth from dominating the people.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed, and the KMT-era state had no policy; nothing in the doctrine decides it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Sun's doctrine treats common religion as one natural force building nations and does not call for state atheism; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Sun's state keeps a judicial branch and a military stage, so abolition is outside the doctrine. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Sun sought a unitary state and assimilation rather than communal power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Livelihood is a state programme to provide basic needs, not a task left to charity.

term-limits.rationale: Sun's design does not mention term limits in the sources I read.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; Sun did fear national extinction through low births.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic, with only the four popular powers stated, and no delegation scheme.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious institutions are outside the doctrine's concerns.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Sun's anti-imperialism opposes foreign influence in China.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; housing appears in livelihood but without rent policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's mixed economy retains private property.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic, though Sun's insistence on sovereignty could imply rejecting foreign weapons on Chinese soil.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sun sought to end foreign concessions and privileges under unequal treaties.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no principle in the doctrine settles it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Land-value tax captures unearned rise in land value for the public, so work not mere ownership should earn.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Sun rejected pacifism, planning military government and revolution.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Sun held nations arise from blood kinship and common customs and revived ancient Chinese virtues from the Great Learning.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The thesis is absent from Sun's doctrine, which treats natural biological groups as basic; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A postmodern feminist claim outside Sun's thought; inferred disagreement.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The KMT honoured revolutionary martyrs and made Sun's testament and tomb into state ritual.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Sun's politics was institutional and developmental rather than a spiritual struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's nationalism focused on unity inside China.

culture-before-state.rationale: Sun sought to overthrow the Qing and build a republic first, with cultural revival alongside.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is outside the doctrine and the sources do not address it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religious interpretation is outside the doctrine and not addressed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Not addressed beyond ending foreign economic control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Sun favoured a unitary state with county autonomy, but administrative mergers for ethnic groups are not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Sun's tutelage state put party leadership above social organisations, though the sources never mention unions; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Sun rejected Marxist class politics and did not require working-class power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Sun's state ran communications and key industries, and county autonomy runs local government, but local utilities are not discussed.

second-chamber.rationale: Sun's five-power design differs from bicameralism; no stated position.

municipal-property.rationale: Sun wanted state ownership of key sectors and private capital, not municipal ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Sun opposed federalism and favoured a unitary state, rejecting confederal arrangements. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

family-wage.rationale: Wage rules are not addressed, though livelihood aims at supporting people's basic needs.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine has no view on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic, with no stance in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; state control of finance suggests disagreement.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; Sun's state order priority implies disagreement.

person-over-state.rationale: Sun held the individual must be pressed into the national whole and liberty curbed for unity.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Sun mixed Confucian morality and materialist drive for subsistence; no clear stance.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Sun favoured a unitary state with county autonomy rather than federal guarantees.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic, and Sun's development plans valued agricultural output but did not address biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: Sun planned ports and railways, but did not discuss urban density or environment.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Sun's nationalism sought one Chinese nation, not racial group organisation.

racial-pride.rationale: Sun's nationalism built on pride in the Chinese nation, but sources are about national not racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Sun planned military government for national defence, but not a stated rule on offensive wars.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Sun gave language as one of five forces forming nations, not the sole one.

communal-electorates.rationale: Sun's nation-building seeks unity under one state, not separate electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Sun feared the great powers would carve up and extinguish China, calling it a hypocolony.

free-public-college.rationale: Sun valued examination and learning, but tuition policy is not in the sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic: Sun's tax idea was the land-value tax, not environmental taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational duty is not discussed, though Datong and national survival themes touch it.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Sun's sources do not discuss gendered values in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: Sun asked powers to devote military budgets to Chinese development, which touches on arms spending, but there is no position on reduction.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; Sun denounced secret unequal treaties implicitly.

capital-controls.rationale: Sun sought to restrain foreign and private capital control of the economy.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The first tutelage stage is military government to unify the country, which implies disarming other armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Sun's programme relied on armies for national defence and the Northern Expedition.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Industrial relations are not discussed beyond Sun's preference for cooperation over struggle.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Specific welfare instruments are not addressed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are anachronistic for Sun, who wanted state investment financed by foreign loans.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Sun denounced unequal treaties and foreign economic control and asked powers to fund Chinese infrastructure.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Sun's revolution overthrew the Qing state and built a new republic, but his five-branch design kept the traditional examination and censorate institutions, so the answer is inferred and mixed.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Sun had a definite blueprint for livelihood, not open economic experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic, with no environmental accounting in the sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: The KMT made the principles dogma with ritual homage and treated the Chinese nation as the highest community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic: student loans did not exist in Sun's context.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Sun applied colonial language to China's relation to foreign powers, not to regions of one state, so the doctrine does not settle this.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Sun grounded Confucian virtues in universal human capacities, but sources do not state this.

public-service-media.rationale: Media policy is not described in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Sun did not discuss religious truth, only religion's role in nation formation.

farm-price-support.rationale: Mao's reading emphasises peasants and land to the tiller, suggesting support for farmers, though price supports are not discussed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic, with no position in the sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: Sun backed a single revolutionary party and class cooperation rather than separate workers' parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed, and nothing in Sun's doctrine of national strengthening supports or opposes it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Property rights for women are not explicitly discussed in the sources.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Sun's single Chinese nation implies treating Sinitic speech as one language, but this is inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; Sun favoured state regulation and direction.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Sun's five-branch design gives no role to customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Sun himself curbed liberty for national goals, but environmental priority is not discussed.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing policy is not addressed in the sources.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Assimilation of minorities into the Han majority implies a common language, but not stated for immigrants.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Union membership rules are not discussed in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Electoral administration is not discussed in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The doctrine is silent on interpretations of religion in law.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Sun said democracy was more than the right to vote, requiring four popular powers and a five-power balance.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; Confucian traditionalism cuts against.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; a strong-state view might allow it, but the sources never raise it.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design of this kind is anachronistic and absent from the sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: Sun's democracy aimed at suffrage for the people, but sources do not specify women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Sun did not claim religion oppresses women, and the sources do not discuss the link.

race-social-construct.rationale: Sun believed in five hereditary biological races.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; the doctrine contains no institutions for gender equality in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Sun's land policy had the state capture land-value gains, not first-claim ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic, and Sun's stress on sovereignty cuts against international courts without settling it.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The doctrine is Confucian-secular and not scriptural; inferred disagreement.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not addressed; Sun's principles do not discuss indigenous self-government arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Sun's alliance with Russia is noted by Mao, but the doctrine does not take sides on bureaucratic planned states.

indirect-election.rationale: Sun's county-up system of people's congresses suggests tiered selection, though he also wanted direct popular powers.

national-church-status.rationale: Religion enters Sun's doctrine only as one nation-forming force, with no church status specified.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Sun favoured a unitary state and assimilation of minorities into the Zhonghua minzu.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed by Sun; his worry about a falling Chinese birth rate points toward encouraging births rather than restricting them.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Sun organised revolution against the Qing and planned military government, so he did not treat initiating force as always wrong.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The KMT made ritual loyalty to Sun and the principles part of party-state life, and its youth organisations followed; the sources do not describe uniforms, so this is inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The sources never address this; Sun stressed ending foreign domination and national unity, but whether he would use local votes for disputed land is not stated.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The sources never address this; Sun wanted foreign powers' hold on China ended, which does not map onto post-colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the livelihood principle, which aims at raising material welfare through state help and development rather than limiting needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The sources never address this; nationalism aimed at one unified Chinese nation, and no settlement policy appears in the sources.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Sun's republic and its general equality of citizens; the sources do not mention conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Nationalism means restoring and unifying the Chinese nation; a spiritual tie to ancestral land is inferred from that, not stated in the sources.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Sun envisaged a republic with a judicial branch in a five-power constitution, so killing without trial is inferred to conflict with it; drug policy is not discussed.

close-ties-china.rationale: Sun sought Soviet help and foreign capital for development, while later KMT governments leaned on the United States, so adherents are split; the question is largely anachronistic.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The nationalism principle aims at a unified Chinese nation including overseas Chinese; support for kin abroad is inferred from this.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Sun's land-value policy returned the unearned rise in land value to the public, which is a form of compensation to all for appropriating land.

self-ownership.rationale: Sun held that individual liberty should be reduced in favour of national liberty, so full individual rights are not central.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Livelihood relies on land-value taxation; consumption taxes are not discussed, so adherents have no clear position.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Livelihood aims at wellbeing for all citizens through state help rather than targeting the poorest only; inferred from its general welfare aim.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The tutelage period put the party in charge, but the democracy principle gives the people four direct powers (election, recall, initiative, referendum), so bypassing groups is not its program.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Livelihood limits private capital and puts key industries under the state to prevent monopoly and extreme inequality.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Sun's program was a secular republic organised on national, not sectarian, lines; this is inferred, not stated directly.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Tridemism draws on Confucian virtues and the Datong ideal while pursuing modern development, combining old values with modern institutions.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Sun's republic aimed at modernising social institutions; support for women's divorce rights is inferred from that, not stated in the sources.

national-resource-control.rationale: Key industries are to be state-run and the nationalism principle is about ending foreign domination of China.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The livelihood principle equalises land rights, taxes land-value gains and limits private capital to prevent extreme inequality, so the resulting pattern matters.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from livelihood's aim of restraining private capital and keeping finance and key industries under state direction; the sources do not mention such a tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic: the doctrine's nationalism concerns foreign domination and unifying Chinese peoples, and takes no stand on racism as an obstacle to disadvantaged groups.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: the party-state's tutelage stage puts national order above individual claims, and the doctrine gives no natural-law view of unjust law.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from livelihood's goal of material plenty shared across the people and its stress on state-led industry; shorter hours are not stated.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: nationalism seeks equal standing for China among nations and an end to foreign domination, which fits a balance of powers.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: it rejects Marxist class struggle and prefers cooperation, so Marx's labour theory is not its basis.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Nationalism and livelihood are paired principles: national strength and people's welfare are pursued together, with cooperation instead of class struggle.

material-over-identity.rationale: Indifferent: the doctrine predates identity politics and pairs economic livelihood with nationalism without ranking against cultural identity issues.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the party-led tutelage state with state-run key industries beside private capital resembles a market under party leadership, though by the Kuomintang rather than a communist party.

missingStatements.text: Government should be divided into five branches, including independent civil-service examination and oversight branches.
missingStatements.rationale: Sun's five-power constitution adds Examination and Control Yuans to the usual three branches, drawn from imperial examinations and the censorate.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Sun's five-yuan constitution; too narrow for the bank.

missingStatements.text: A country should pass through a period of tutelage under a revolutionary party before full constitutional democracy.
missingStatements.rationale: Sun's Fundamentals of National Reconstruction set military rule, political tutelage and then constitutional government, read as KMT party leadership.

missingStatements.text: Increases in land value caused by social development should go to the public rather than to private owners.
missingStatements.rationale: Sun adapted Henry George's land-value ideas so that rising values after development benefit the state through taxation and a buyback right.

notes: Answers reflect Sun's 1924 doctrine as the KMT mainstream used it. The Communist "New Three Principles" reading differs on class struggle and the Soviet alliance. Many answers are low confidence because Sun wrote before most statements arose; sources I could open did not include the full 1924 lectures.
